newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope undergoes appendix surgery-hospital sources.
newsitem.headline: Pope undergoes appendix surgery-hospital sources.

text.p: Doctors began operating on Pope John Paul on Tuesday to remove his appendix, hospital sources said.
The 76-year-old Pope, who has had major abdominal surgery three times since 1981, was taken into the operating theatre at Rome's Gemelli hospital at around 7.15 a.m. (0515 GMT)

The surgery was announced by the Vatican last month when it said recurrent inflammation of the appendix was the cause of three bouts of "intestinal fever" the Polish-born Pope has suffered since Christmas.

The Pope was admitted to the Gemelli on Sunday night. The hospital has said it will release a medical bulletin at around 11 a.m. (0900 GMT). Italian radio said the operation was expected to last about two hours.

The team of doctors, working in a ninth-floor operating theatre, is led by Professor Francesco Crucitti, the surgeon who saved the Pope's life in 1981 after he was shot by Turkish gunman Mehmet Ali Agca in St Peter's Square.
